failures_and_limits: The first GUI campaign passed all 114 control steps, then failed because its window or daemon exited during the idle-resource sample. Empty logs and absent new crash reports do not establish why. The old driver did not preserve which process or its exit code. The diagnostic change now reports both exit codes and the completed sample count. The original failure remains unexplained; rerun success does not resolve it.
The diagnostic repeat used identical 796270a executables; only the Python idle-sample error text changed. This driver-only change followed the pinned clean build.

Diagnostic idle ps CPU median was 33.2 percent for the window and 0 for the daemon, with window median RSS 178036736 bytes. Active physical user interaction was uncontrolled. These are short observations, not idle-performance acceptance. Claude independently observed high memory at 100 fixture agents on an older package; investigation is ongoing.
The original spurious conflict channel in the installed daemon is retained. This source fix suppresses future removed-root notifications after replacement; it does not rewrite historical channels.

Native workflows invoke rendered callbacks. Notification routing uses private IPC and CLI activation, not physical Notification Center clicks. Provider submitted-input parity and idle wake remain open.
